ALMONTE Vice-Governor Province of Misamis Occidental Capitol, Oroquieta City Dear Vice-Governor Almonte: This has reference to your letter dated 24 November 2021 addressed to Gov. Philip Tan, informing the latter that Resolution No. 680-21 cannot be held in abeyance. Resolution No. 680-21 basically is a recommendation for preventive suspension against Mayor Alicia Ty and Vice-Mayor Rolando Manuel C. Ty of Plaridel, Misamis Occidental. At the outset, it is noted that the Department is only copy furnished in your letter. Be that as it may, the fact that the Department was copy furnished may be interpreted to mean that the parties are requesting the Department to clarify whether the actions of the contending parties are in accordance with RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991. Based on the documents forwarded to the Central Office, it appears that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Misamis Occidental adopted Resolution No. 680-21 recommending the preventive suspension of Mayor Alicia Ty and Vice-Mayor Manuel C. Ty of Plaridel, Misamis Occidental. However, Governor Philip Tan held in abeyance the implementation of the preventive suspension for the following grounds, which we quoted in toto: "I. 2. 3. The case as far presented may not provide adequate basis to reasonably place respondents under preventive suspension... I cannot see any sufficient basis to justify the preventive specially so now that we are in a pandemic and in a state of national calamity and public health emergency. The simultaneous preventive suspension of these top officials may just disrupt the LGU's normal operations, much to the detriment of public service. We may safely assume that it is not easy to replace them in their respective functions as those substituting them may be taking over for the first time. The General Welfare Clause and Section 465 (b)(l )(vii) of the Local Government Code." "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

May it be respectfully informed that the issue raised in the case at hand, that is, whether or not the Governor may hold in abeyance the implementation of the preventive suspension against Mayor Alicia Ty and Vice-Mayor Rolando Manuel C. Ty for reasons above-cited, has already been discussed and settled in DILG Legal Opinion No. 44, series of 2004, pertinent portion of which reads: "In fine. as to whether or not the power to impose preventive suspension is ministerial or discretionary function on the part of the f the consid r view that h uthori over r r ma or the local chief executives (Governor/Mayor) to impose preventive suspension is purely ministerial since the disciplinary authority over errinq municipal or baranqav elective officials is the Sanqquniang Panlalawigan. Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sanggunianq Bayan. as the case may be. Hence. after the sanqqunian shall have determin ed the necessity to warrant the imposition of preventive suspension. the same must be implemented by the local chief executive concerned. Moreover, the Court of Appeals ruling in the case of Gov. Francisco T. Matugas, Petitioner versus The Honorable Floripinas C. Buyser, as Judge of Branch 31 Regional Trial Court of Dapa, Surigao del Norte and Mayor Alma G. Navarro, Respondents in CA-G.R. SP No. 55563 is instructive where it was held that 'the authority to determine whether the evidence warrants the preventive suspension of an elective municipal officia/ finds support in the ruling in Espiritu vs. Me/gar that the office or body that is invested with the power of removal or suspension should be the sole judge of the necessity and sufficiency of the cause. Moreover, to give to the provincial governor the authority to determine whether preventive suspension is warranted on the grounds that the evidence of guilt is strong and given the gravity of the offense, there is great probability that the continuance in office of the respondent could influence the witnesses or pose a threat to the safety and integrity of the records and other evidence without prior recommendation by the Sangguniang Pan/a/awigan, would constitute undue interference on the authority of said body to investigate and discipline elective municipal officials and preempt the latter's decision on the administrative case. " As such, please be informed that if the Mayor is beinq directed by the Spngqvnian to implement its order, resolution, decision or judgment issued pursuant to the exercise of its quasi-judicial powers conferred by Section 61 of the Local Government Code. it is the ministerial duty of the Mayor to execute the same ane he has no discretion to determine the propriety of the implementation of the order, resolution or iudqment or decision. The service or implementation of the order. resolution or decision has to be made without unnecessary delay so that after beinq duly informed. the respondent can immediately take steps to protect his interests by filinq an appeal or apply for other appropriate relief. The r ven •ve s nsi c efus I o the un- i M r im Ie nt be considered as obstruction of justice and therefore would be tantamount to grave misconduct for which he may be administratively (Emphasis Supplied) A copy of the aforesaid DILG Legal Opinion No. 44, series of 2004 is hereto attached for ease of reference. As such, upon receipt of the Resolution recommending to Governor Tan the imposition of preventive suspension upon Mayor Alicia Ty and Vice-Mayor Rolando Manuel C. Ty, the Governor should immediately implement the same. His refusal to immediately Page 2 of 3

implement the same is considered as obstruction of justice and therefore would be tantamount to grave misconduct for which he may be administratively sanctioned. So far, we have yet to receive any directive imposing a moratorium on the suspension of local elective officials due to the on-going COVID-19 pandemic. Rather, the more viable reasons for the non-implementation of the preventive suspension against the respondents are the upcominq election period (which starts on January 9, 2022 and ends on June 8, 2022) and Section 62 (c) 1 of the Local Government Code of 1991. May we take this opportunity however to clarify that under Section 261 (x) of the Omnibus Election Code, what is being prohibited is the suspension of local elective officials without the approval or clearance of the Commission on Elections (COMELEC). Hence, at the onset of the election period on January 9, 2022, the official so directed to implement the order of suspension should seek the COMELEC's clearance prior to the implementation thereof. Pending such COMELEC clearance, he cannot yet implement the suspension order. On the other hand, if the COMELEC gives its clearance, the said official can already implement the suspension order. Lastly, it may be well to emphasize that there are mechanisms already in place for the designation/appointment of the acting officials in case of temporary vacancies in the respective positions of the respondents due to the implementation of their preventive suspensions. This opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same, and rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . DILG MARL GAN for Local Government OUSLG/MLl/LLLs-LRALLD/rrao/clp Copy furnished. HON. PHILIP T.
